theory.intro: A tangent to a circle is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact, and the two tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point are always equal in length. These two facts let you find unknown angles and lengths in diagrams built from tangents and radii.
facts: A tangent meets the radius at the point of contact at $90^{\circ}$: if $T$ is the point of contact of tangent $TP$, then $\angle OTP = 90^{\circ}$.
The two tangents drawn to a circle from the same external point are equal in length: if $PT$ and $PQ$ are tangents from $P$, then $PT = PQ$.
Because $PT = PQ$, $\triangle TPQ$ is isosceles, so its base angles are equal.
In quadrilateral $OTPQ$ (radius, tangent, tangent, radius), the two right angles at $T$ and $Q$ mean the angles at $O$ and $P$ are supplementary: $\angle TOQ + \angle TPQ = 180^{\circ}$.
steps: Mark the right angle(s) between each tangent and its radius at the point of contact.
Mark any tangent lengths that are equal because they are drawn from the same external point.
Use angle sum, Pythagoras’ theorem, or the isosceles triangle formed by equal tangents to find the unknown.

foundation.solution_text:
$\angle OTP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$x + 90^{\circ} + 55^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle OTP$)
$x = 35^{\circ}$

$PQ = PT$ (tangents drawn to a circle from an external point are equal)
$PQ = 9\text{ cm}$

$PT = PQ$ (tangents from an external point are equal)
$\triangle TPQ$ is isosceles, so its base angles are equal
$2x + 70^{\circ} = 180^{\circ}$ (angle sum of $\triangle TPQ$)
$x = 55^{\circ}$

$\angle OTP = \angle OQP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangents meet radii at $90^{\circ}$)
$x + 90^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} + 64^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$ (angle sum of quadrilateral $OTPQ$)
$x = 116^{\circ}$

$\angle OTP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$x^{2} = 3^{2} + 4^{2}$ (Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle OTP$)
$x^{2} = 25$
$x = 5\text{ cm}$

$\angle OTP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$13^{2} = 5^{2} + x^{2}$ (Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle OTP$)
$169 = 25 + x^{2}$
$x^{2} = 144$
$x = 12\text{ cm}$

mastery.solution_text:
In $\triangle PTO$ and $\triangle PQO$:
$\angle OTP = \angle OQP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangents meet radii at $90^{\circ}$)
$OT = OQ$ (equal radii)
$OP = OP$ (common)
$\therefore \triangle PTO \equiv \triangle PQO$ (RHS)
$PT = PQ$ (matching sides of congruent triangles)

(a) $\angle OTP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$OP^{2} = 9^{2} + 12^{2}$ (Pythagoras' theorem in $\triangle OTP$)
$OP^{2} = 225$
$OP = 15\text{ cm}$
(b) $\angle OTP = \angle OQP = 90^{\circ}$ (tangents meet radii at $90^{\circ}$)
$\angle TPQ + 90^{\circ} + 90^{\circ} + 100^{\circ} = 360^{\circ}$ (angle sum of quadrilateral $OTPQ$)
$\angle TPQ = 80^{\circ}$

Let $PX = PZ = p$, $QX = QY = q$ and $RY = RZ = r$ (tangents from each vertex are equal)
$p + q = 13$ ($PQ$)
$q + r = 14$ ($QR$)
$r + p = 15$ ($RP$)
Adding all three: $2(p+q+r) = 42$
$p + q + r = 21$
$r = 21 - 13 = 8$, so $q = 14 - 8 = 6$
$QY = q = 6\text{ cm}$
